name: place_structure
summary: Place any structure a kit builds (light, sign, device, frame, wall, tank, rocket part) by prefab, at a point with a turn, build state, label and colour; several placements are one job. Checked as the player's cursor checks. Dry run by default; confirm to build. free is a cheat.

help.text: With placements, label, color and so on go in each placement. Cost: every build state's items up to the state built (state 0 is the kit), from the player's inventory or from_id. Cables, pipes and chutes are placed as exactly the piece given; place_cables, place_pipes and place_chutes choose pieces. The dry run describes each placement: position, cost, ports, layout.
help.keys: job_id, status, ready, problems [], warnings [], placements [], materials [], result, error.

position.summary: How at snaps, and setting a piece down.
position.text: at is a point in the cell, snapped as the cursor snaps it (a 2 m device snaps to its cell's centre). When a 0.5 m device (not a cable, pipe or chute) cannot be built at the point given, it is tried set down on the surface behind it, as the cursor's ray lands: the floor below for a standing device, the face at its back for a mounted one; only onto a surface that is there, so a taken spot is refused rather than moved. resolved.at_how says when and why. A piece placed on a cell face sits on the face opposite its facing.

ports.summary: The ports a placement would have.
ports.text: For a device, or another thing with ends that is not a cable, pipe or chute piece (an in-line tank, a passive vent): ports [{index, at (the cell a piece joining it would stand in), toward (the end that piece needs), type, role, network_id (null)}] where the ports would land at that position and turn, in grid_survey's shape.

layout.summary: The layout preview of each placement.
layout.text: layout {footprint {small_cells (a count unless include_footprint_cells), large_cells, body {origin, render_box, centre_offset, grid_box, grid_cells}, mount {plane, outward, axes, min, max}}, sections {walls, count, crosses_seam}, conflicts [{code, level info, warning or problem, message, reference_id}], port_checks [{index, at, toward, type, role, flow, occupant, joins, would_join_network, blocked, in_door_keepout}]}. A report that is not ready leaves layouts out unless verbose.

conflicts.text: visual_overlap: its mesh box and another thing's run more than 0.1 m into each other, or one lies inside the other (flush neighbours only touch; a thing sharing a cell is skipped). crosses_section_seam: its mesh spans more than one 2 m section though it could fit one (a warning; not for pieces wider than a section). in_door_keepout, crosses_window, blocks_route_cells (it stands in a neighbour port's joining cell), front_blocked, controls_blocked (its controls face a device, frame body or wall right in front, or a plate, frame or thing covering a quarter of that side within 0.5 m: controls sunk in or facing down onto a floor), clips_surface (its mesh box runs more than 0.1 m into a wall, floor or ceiling plate or a frame's body it does not rest on: built lying, sunk into the floor), faces_out_of_room, not_upright (info for prefabs normally built lying, the in-line tanks).

prefab.description: Prefab name (StructureWallLight, as find_things and looking_at report them) or prefab hash.

at.description: A point in the cell, snapped as the cursor snaps it; or a crosshair, relative or look-face form (see positions).

rotation.description: [x, y, z] degrees, multiples of 90 (see turns/rotation).

facing.description: Where the piece's front points: an axis or a named facing (see turns/facing).

up.description: Where its top points, with facing or face; default +y, or +z when facing is vertical.

face.description: Face-placed pieces (walls): the face of the cell it sits on (see turns/face).

orient.description: Choose the turn by intent instead of rotation, facing, face and up (see turns/orient).

mount.description: wall, floor, ceiling, or an axis: the side the surface it rests on is on.

upright.description: Default true: its visual top should point +y.

controls_toward.description: Where its controls should face: an axis, "room", "player", a point or {reference_id}.

role.description: Input, Input2, Output, Output2, Waste or None.

index.description: A port by its index (describe_prefab lists them).

type.description: Pipe, PowerAndData, Chute... (part of the name).

ports.description: Ports to point, each {role, type, toward}.

flow.description: Inputs should face from, outputs to.

above_floor_m.description: Set its bottom this many metres above the floor below at (see positions/above_floor).

build_state.description: finished (default), first (as a kit leaves it) or a state index.

label.description: A name, as the Labeller writes it.

color.description: A colour name or index (paint lists them).

free.description: Place without materials; creative worlds only (not_creative otherwise). A cheat. Default false.

allow_door_keepout.description: Default false: a small-grid piece with a cell in a door's keep-out (its face and the configured band either side inside its rectangle) is refused with in_door_keepout; true makes it a warning.

verbose.description: With job_id: the whole job; with a confirmed run: the whole preflight; with a dry run: layouts a refused report leaves out.
